A1.justification: Both are complete 19-page versions of the same P2 Law study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices can be matched despite renumbering and the addition of Appendix C in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original post-training losses and scaling-law fitting and generalization results for pruned Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 models, including Tables 2–4 and appendix figures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experimental losses and scaling-law evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The scaling-law functional forms, L1 selection, Levenberg–Marquardt fitting, and pruning/post-training procedures are retained. Changing the inspiration citation from SP-LoRA to LoRS leaves the masked weight-update equation in Appendix B.3 unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use SlimPajama for the same language-model post-training and loss-prediction tasks, with depth, width, and 2:4 semi-structured pruning. The new discussion of 70B models concerns future work, not added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the L1/L2/L3 comparison, and Table 4 retains L1 against the OpenAI-law-based L4/L5 alternatives. The revised sparse-training inspiration citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 revises the reported batch size from 256k to 262k tokens; learning rate, token budgets, metrics, and the 80/20 checkpoint split remain unchanged. This does not establish a rerun. v3's broader wording about excluding Llama-3.1-8B conflicts with retained depth-pruning generalization results, including Figure 23a.

E4.justification: New Appendix C briefly reports that approximately 2e-5 is experimentally optimal across 0.5B–8B models, adding a limited finding about learning-rate selection across scales. No tested-rate grid or comparative losses accompany it. Existing parameterization comparisons and the width-pruning anomaly analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, explicit seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. v3 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes gamma for the Llama-3 L1 depth-pruning fit from +1.08 to -1.08. Appendix C also newly asserts an experimental learning-rate optimum near 2e-5. Tables 2–4 retain identical scores, and matched loss curves retain their data despite display adjustments.

T1.justification: The loss definitions, three necessary conditions, ASD formula, candidate scaling laws, and appendix pruning equations are unchanged. v3 explicitly explains omissions already present in the 2:4 parameterizations. The corrected fitted coefficient in Table 5 does not introduce a new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the first post-pruning scaling-law claim, ASD contribution, and generalization claims. Describing Figure 1 as accurately fitting rather than predicting checkpoints clarifies the illustration without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: The limitations section replaces the warning about transfer to other architectures, including MoE, with a computational-resource and model-scale limitation plus a projected 70B training cost. Its 'fewer than 8B' wording is imprecise given retained 8B experiments. Existing width-anomaly and larger-model slope interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds hyperparameter-selection rationale, and Section 4.3.1 explicitly states the fixed pruning-rate or model-size controls for generalization. Table 5 corrects a parameter needed to reproduce the fitted law. Hardware, reported 500-hour training time, and Appendix A's future data-release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds McCandlish et al. (2018) and further discusses Kaplan et al. (2020) to justify training settings. Attribution for the unchanged sparse-update mechanism changes from SP-LoRA to LoRS. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v3 corrects ADS to ASD, refines local explanations, consolidates the three generalization-results subsections under Section 4.3.2, and adds Appendix C. Affiliations, contribution notes, and acknowledgments are updated, while the main narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 Figures 7–9 become v3 Figure 7(a–c). Computational axes are relabeled 'Compute', several vertical ranges change, and appendix captions clarify fitting versus validation. Figure 15c introduces a legend labeling the model Qwen-2.5-1.5B although its caption still identifies Qwen-2.5-3B.

improvement.justification: Table 5's sign correction makes the fitted law consistent with its stated pruning-rate behavior, improving reproducibility. Added settings explanations and clearer fitting/validation captions provide smaller clarity gains. These support a limited net improvement despite the removed MoE caveat and new model-label/exclusion ambiguities; the main empirical validation remains unchanged.
